claims.text:
The name Fengel seems to be in Noldorin, but its meaning is unclear.
An earlier name for the character was Eär.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Shaping of Middle-earth, "I. Prose Fragments Following the Lost Tales: (i) [Turlin and the exiles of Gondolin]", pp. 4-5

claims.text: An earlier name for the character was Eär.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Shaping of Middle-earth, "I. Prose Fragments Following the Lost Tales: (i) [Turlin and the exiles of Gondolin]", pp. 4-5

claims.text: In The Lay of the Fall of Gondolin, from c. 1920, Fengel replaced Peleg as the name of Tuor's father.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Lays of Beleriand, "II. Poems Early Abandoned: The Lay of the Fall of Gondolin", p. 145
claims.section: section == Other versions of the legendarium == > Early legendarium

claims.text: The name Fengel also appears as the name of Tuor himself, in a fragment of an alliterative Lay of Eärendel from c. 1925.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Lays of Beleriand, "II. Poems Early Abandoned: Fragment of an alliterative Lay of Eärendel", p. 141
claims.section: section == Other versions of the legendarium == > Early legendarium

claims.text: In the later legendarium from The Lord of the Rings, Fengel was the name of the fifteenth king of Rohan.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix A, "The House of Eorl", "The Kings of the Mark", p. 1,069
claims.section: section == Other versions of the legendarium == > Later legendarium
